stem: In a young infant with acute lower-airway disease, which feature most directly increases airway resistance?
explanation: Smaller diameter airways increase airway resistance. In infants, relatively narrow airways mean even small amounts of swelling or secretions can markedly obstruct airflow.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a large occiput can affect head position and airway alignment, but it does not directly increase airway resistance.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because smaller diameter airways markedly increase resistance to airflow, especially in infants with acute airway inflammation or secretions.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a compliant chest wall affects work of breathing and lung volume maintenance rather than directly increasing airway resistance.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because fewer alveoli affect gas exchange capacity, not airway resistance.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a higher proportion of foetal haemoglobin affects oxygen affinity, not airway resistance.
